one_line_contribution: The claim that a retrieved memory item's marginal value is a property of the (item, instruction) pair rather than of the item, operationalized as a unit-level REDUNDANT/NOVEL/CONFLICTING labeling against the task instruction, and tested by token-matched surgical deletion with a decoy-instruction placebo plus a novel-units-per-token retrieval rule.
closest_prior_work: Two clusters. (a) For the phenomenon, the ACL 2026 experience-following study the proposal itself names: it already establishes helps/hurts/low-value under similarity retrieval, so this proposal owns only the mechanism, and it correctly concedes that. (b) The more dangerous cluster is one the proposal never checks: query-conditioned context compression and instruction-conditioned retrieval. RECOMP (Xu et al. 2023), LLMLingua-2 and Provence-style pruners already delete context spans that the conditioning text makes unnecessary, at sub-item granularity, at matched token budgets; Promptriever/FollowIR/INSTRUCTOR already condition retrieval scoring on an instruction string rather than the bare query. Swapping the conditioning text from 'query' to 'agent instruction' and the objective from 'relevance' to 'non-entailment' is a small, natural delta on top of that machinery, and a reviewer who knows that literature will read Part 3 as instruction-conditioned RECOMP applied to a memory bank. Sufficient Context (ICLR 2025) supplies the conceptual frame ('does the context add what is missing') and the proposal's own defense — that 'missing' there is relative to question plus parametric knowledge — is thin, because parametric knowledge is exactly the analogue of 'what the prompt already says'.
strongest_objection: Part 1, the predictive core, is powered as if it had 1,000 balanced binary observations, but its outcomes (fix and break of S1 vs S0) are rare events whose rate the design only bounds from below at 6% movement in *either* direction (precheck, 150 dev instances). This track's own prior result was a bank that fixed zero items and broke six to seven. So a bank that passes the gate entirely on breaks yields literally zero fix events, and prediction 2's 'novel-unit count predicts fixes' becomes untestable while the study proceeds. Even in a favorable case, 6-10% total movement over 500 instances x 2 conditions gives on the order of 20-40 fix events and a similar number of breaks, against a mixed-effects logistic model carrying seven fixed effects (three unit counts, injected tokens, retrieval score, instance difficulty, embedding proxy) plus instance random effects. That is roughly 3-5 events per variable, an order of magnitude short of what the stated 0.22 standardized-log-odds detection assumes, and the 'removing the three unit counts drops explained deviance by 25% relative' test is essentially unconstrained at that event count. The conflicting channel is worse: no expected prevalence of CONFLICTING units is stated anywhere, the 400-pair validation set will likely contain very few of them (so the kappa>0.6 gate can pass while the CONFLICTING class is unvalidated), and S5 (drop-conflicting) was cut, so the break half of the mechanism -- the half that matters most given the track's headline harm result -- has no causal arm and an unpowered regression coefficient. Secondary but nearly as damaging: the I_short/I_long manipulation that carries prediction 1 is confounded three ways. I_long is simultaneously (i) more redundant with the bank, (ii) more accurate on this task distribution, hence lower headroom for memory to fix anything, and (iii) longer, which by the proposal's own cited Context Length Alone Hurts should depress performance independent of content. A collapse in S1-S0 from I_short to I_long is exactly what a pure ceiling/headroom account predicts with no unit-level mechanism, and baseline (iv) is explicitly counted as confirmation rather than as the rival explanation it is. Third: predictions 1 and 5 are in tension. Prediction 1 says memory's gain collapses under I_long; Part 3 is run under I_long only and prediction 5 demands complementarity beat top-k by >=5 points there. If S1-S0 under I_long is near zero, no reallocation of which items get injected can move accuracy 5 points unless top-k is actively harmful under I_long by several points, which is neither predicted nor powered. Fourth, an arithmetic inconsistency: prediction 1 caps REDUNDANT at <=15% of units under I_short, so S2 can delete at most ~15% of tokens there, yet prediction 3 asserts S2 cuts injected tokens by >=40% while being equivalent to S1 'pooled across instruction conditions'. Pooling a condition where S2 is a near-no-op by construction into an equivalence test biases straight toward declaring equivalence, and the same pooling makes the token-savings headline unachievable as stated.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Compute Part 1's power on the fix and break event counts, not on 1,000 instances, and make the precheck gate the *fix* rate specifically (e.g. >=8% of dev instances fixed under at least one instruction) rather than movement in either direction; if fixes cannot be made numerous enough, drop the seven-regressor model for a pre-registered two- or three-term model and state the CONFLICTING prevalence you expect, oversampling conflicting pairs into the 400-pair validation set so that class is actually validated. (2) Add a third instruction condition that breaks the confound: an I_long_control matched to I_long in length, register and (as far as possible) no-memory accuracy but produced so that its content does not overlap the bank -- e.g. optimized on a disjoint training slice or on a different guidance axis. Relationality is only established if the same items go redundant under I_long and stay novel under I_long_control while the S1-S0 gain drops only in the former. Without this, the S7 decoy controls the deletion arms but nothing controls the manipulation that prediction 1 rests on. (3) Restore an S5-type drop-conflicting arm, or accept and state that the break/CONFLICTING branch is descriptive only and remove it from the headline three-way claim. (4) Report the S2-vs-S1 equivalence and the token-savings figure per instruction condition, never pooled. (5) Move at least one Part 3 budget to I_short, or state and power the specific mechanism by which complementarity wins under I_long (avoided harm, not added fixes), and report the S1-S0 ceiling alongside every rule comparison so the reader can see how much room any rule had.
missing_baseline: Two. First and most important, the length- and headroom-matched control instruction described above -- the proposal has an instruction-level placebo nowhere, only a deletion-level one (S7), so the single manipulation carrying the central relationality claim is uncontrolled. Second, a single-call LLM instruction-conditioned pruner: put the instruction and the top-k items in one frontier-or-local model call and ask it to delete what the instruction already says, at the same token budget as S2/complementarity. The proposal cut LLM-compressor baselines on the grounds that MMR tests the same thing more cleanly, which is wrong -- MMR is item-vs-item and tests the reference-set claim, while the LLM pruner is instruction-conditioned and tests the *instrument* claim from the strong side. As written, the instrument is defended only against a deliberately weak competitor (embedding cosine plus Jaccard); a reviewer will note that the interesting question is whether atomic decomposition plus DeBERTa-MNLI beats one prompt, and that question is not asked. A third, cheaper omission: appending the NOVEL units directly to the instruction instead of injecting items, which is the natural test of risk factor 4 (does guidance need episodic form) and would cost one extra arm.
preprint_collision: Above average for this kind of check and clearly a real search, with an honest OpenReview caveat and a correct concession that the ACL 2026 experience-following paper removes the right to claim the phenomenon. But it is scoped to one niche -- agent-memory harm -- and therefore misses the literature where the actual method already lives. It contains no search of context/prompt compression (RECOMP, LLMLingua/LLMLingua-2, Provence and their 2026 successors), which does conditioned sub-item deletion at matched token budgets, and none of instruction-conditioned retrieval (Promptriever, FollowIR, INSTRUCTOR and follow-ups), which already scores candidates against an instruction string rather than a query. Instruction-conditioned redundancy pruning of a memory bank sits directly between those two lines, and the proposal's own predicted failure mode -- the cheap embedding-overlap proxy wins -- is precisely the result that compression work would lead you to expect. The proposal's stated risk that 'instruction-aware dedup appears as an appendix ablation in a contemporaneous context-compilation preprint' is, in my judgment, understated rather than nontrivial. Separately, four of the seven cited items are arXiv identifiers I cannot verify (2601.07470, 2605.09330, 2606.19847, 2607.05936); I do not treat that as bad faith, but a submission version should carry titles plus venues and the authors should confirm those IDs resolve, since a check whose load-bearing citations cannot be resolved by a reviewer establishes less novelty than it appears to. Net: not a collision I can name, but the check is under-scoped in the direction that matters most, so it does not fully discharge the novelty burden.
